Fixed: added Metadata::get_range_for_channel(); file.rs column-extraction loop now masks integer parameters to ($PnR.next_power_of_two() - 1) before building the DataFrame column. Test added in fcs/src/write.rs (pnr_mask_strips_garbage_high_bits_from_int16_data) confirmed red against pre-fix code, green after. Full fcs suite (76 tests) + clippy clean.

Fixed record stride math: calculate_bytes_per_event() now sums raw $PnB bit widths across all parameters and rounds up once (ceil(sum(bits)/8)), instead of rounding each parameter individually before summing. The old approach overcounted for bit-packed (non-byte-aligned $PnB) records, e.g. 8x $PnB=10 params: correct=ceil(80/8)=10 bytes, old buggy=8*ceil(10/8)=16 bytes. Added a dedicated bit-packed read path (parse_bit_packed_data + a hand-rolled MSB-first BitReader in file.rs) used only when at least one parameter's $PnB isn't a multiple of 8; the existing byte-aligned fast/variable-width paths are untouched for the common case. New test bit_packed_pnb10_record_uses_correct_stride_and_decodes hand-packs 8x10-bit channels and round-trips through calculate_bytes_per_event + Fcs::open. Verified true red state via git-stash-isolated pre-fix code (test failed with predicted 16 vs 10). Also fixed a pre-existing clippy manual_div_ceil lint on the unrelated (dead-code, zero call sites) get_bytes_for_bits. cargo test -p flow-fcs --lib: 77/77 pass. cargo clippy -p flow-fcs --lib --tests: 0 errors, no new warnings. Known limitation (documented in code): bit order is spec-derived (MSB-first) and internally consistent but not validated against a real vendor's on-disk bit order, since FCS 3.2 deprecated bit-packing specifically because vendors disagreed on this.

Implemented $NEXTDATA traversal via a new Fcs::open_all(path) -> Result<Vec<Fcs>>, alongside the unchanged Fcs::open() (still returns only dataset 1, same cost as before for the ~100% common single-dataset case).

Design: factored open()'s body into a private parse_one_dataset(file_access: AccessWrapper, header: Header) -> Result<(Self, usize)>, which now also reads back $NEXTDATA's value (0 if absent) after building the Fcs. open() calls it once and discards the offset; open_all() loops while next_offset != 0, with a HashSet-based cycle guard against a corrupt file whose chain loops back on an already-visited TEXT offset.

Key discovery before writing any code: $NEXTDATA has no dedicated IntegerKeyword variant — parse_fixed_keywords (keyword/parsing.rs) has no match arm for "NEXTDATA", so it always falls through to StringKeyword::Other. parse_one_dataset reads it via metadata.get_string_keyword("$NEXTDATA") + get_str().trim().parse::<usize>(), not get_integer_keyword (which would never find it).

The harder problem: only dataset 1 has the fixed 58-byte primary HEADER; dataset 2+ has no repeated HEADER, only a new TEXT segment (pointed to by $NEXTDATA, confirmed as an absolute file offset per version.rs's keyword docs) followed by its own DATA segment. There's no explicit "TEXT end" for these datasets — it can only be derived as ($BEGINDATA - 1), and $BEGINDATA is itself a keyword/value pair inside the TEXT segment being bounded. Solved with two small helpers:
- find_begindata_offset(mmap, text_start): a bounded, early-stopping delimiter tokenizer (mirrors Metadata::from_mmap's keyword/value alternation exactly) that stops the instant it finds $BEGINDATA, so it never risks reading into DATA bytes (which could coincidentally contain the delimiter byte value).
- header_for_dataset_at(mmap, text_start, version): packages that into a synthetic Header { text_offset: text_start..=(begin_data-1), data_offset: 0..=0, ... } — data_offset is 0..=0 deliberately, because store_raw_data_as_dataframe already has an existing fallback (checks metadata's $BEGINDATA/$ENDDATA when header.data_offset is 0) that this reuses for free, so dataset 2+ needed no changes to the DATA-parsing path at all.

Test (write.rs, TDD red->green): hand-built a synthetic two-dataset file — dataset 1 with a real primary HEADER whose $NEXTDATA points at dataset 2's TEXT start, dataset 2 appended directly as TEXT+DATA with no second HEADER. Converged dataset 1's TEXT/DATA layout AND its $NEXTDATA value together in one loop (changing $NEXTDATA's digit count shifts dataset 1's TEXT length, which shifts where dataset 2 starts). Asserted open() still returns only dataset 1's values, and open_all() returns both datasets' distinct values in order. Confirmed this failed to compile before implementation (Fcs::open_all didn't exist).

Verification: cargo test -p flow-fcs --lib: 78/78 passed (77 pre-existing + 1 new). cargo clippy -p flow-fcs --lib --tests: 0 errors, 0 new warnings (33 pre-existing warnings elsewhere in the crate, none touching the new code).

Design rationale for keeping open()/open_all() separate rather than merging: eager-cost avoidance (a caller wanting only dataset 1 doesn't pay to parse+DataFrame-build datasets 2..N), failure isolation (a bad dataset 2 doesn't invalidate a good dataset 1), and call-site ergonomics (no .first() boilerplate needed at every existing single-dataset call site). Matches what flowCore and FlowIO independently converged on.

Follow-up: flow-crates-vjd (multi-dataset UX decision at the app layer — cycle/merge/keep-separate) is now unblocked.

Won't-fix: existing behavior (explicit Err on $DATATYPE=A) is already the correct failure mode. FCS deprecated the ASCII datatype specifically because vendor implementations disagreed on interpretation, and no supported instrument/tool in this ecosystem emits it — rejecting it is a deliberate spec-driven decision, not a gap. Changes made: (1) updated the doc comment on FcsDataType::from_keyword_str (fcs/src/datatype.rs) to state explicitly that ASCII is deprecated by spec and intentionally unsupported, referencing this issue, so it reads as a decision rather than an oversight; (2) added a unit test (from_keyword_str_rejects_deprecated_ascii_datatype) confirming the Err path, since none existed anywhere in the crate previously. Verified: cargo test -p flow-fcs --lib passes 79/79 (was 78 before this test addition); cargo clippy -p flow-fcs --lib --tests shows zero new warnings (only pre-existing, unrelated warnings in the analyze_benchmarks bin).
